## Re-review — Final validation — Phase 1 + Phase 2

At 1eb5f2721e09773958b22e5b2133bff0fcfea72e, a new regression test verifies that the public FFI can list and read `0xface` as text, and the Swift DPNS listing and vote-state reads now run off the main actor. Rust workspace tests and the Kotlin SDK build and tests passed in CI; Swift SDK build and tests and PR Hygiene were still pending.

🔴 1 blocking | 🟡 3 suggestion(s)

### Still open from earlier rounds (1)

- 🔴 **Blocking**: Keep DPNS contest addressing and name parsing in Rust — `packages/swift-sdk/SwiftExampleApp/SwiftExampleApp/Views/QueryDetailView.swift:469-478` ([thread](https://github.com/dashpay/platform/pull/6034#discussion_r4651948881))

### Disputed — left to maintainers (1)

- 🔴 **Blocking**: Return reusable poll selectors only when the path is complete and lossless — `packages/rs-sdk-ffi/src/contested_resource/queries/resources.rs:243-254` ([thread](https://github.com/dashpay/platform/pull/6034#discussion_r4651948872))

<details>
<summary>Follow-up candidates (optional) (1)</summary>

New non-blocking observations on code unchanged since the last full review. No inline threads are opened for them and later reviews do not repeat them: fix forward or track separately if they are worth it.

**🟡 Suggestion: Keep the full-name normalizer private**
`packages/rs-sdk/src/platform/dpns_usernames/mod.rs:58`

The FFI now calls the bare-label homograph converter again, so every caller of `normalize_dpns_label` is within this module or its children. Restore the helper's private visibility and describe the optional `.dash` suffix handling directly in the public vote-state method's rustdoc. That keeps the behavior documented without adding a separate public API commitment.

<sub>source: `gpt-6.2-sol` (phase2-reviewer: general, architecture-layering, ffi-engineer, rust-quality)</sub>

</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for all review comments with AI agents</summary>

```
These findings are from an automated code review (PastaClaw). How to work through them:
- Verify each finding against the code; fix only what is real, as narrowly as the finding.
- If a finding is wrong, decline it on its thread in one or two sentences; the bot answers once and stops.
- To defer one, link a tracking issue on its thread (or reply asking the bot to file one).
- Suggestions don't block the merge, but most are worth fixing in this PR; judge each on its merits.
- Keep the PR's scope; don't grow it to satisfy hardening suggestions.
- Carried items were raised in an earlier round: read the thread first, and don't re-fix what you already fixed, declined or deferred there. Disputed and deferred items are already handled and are not listed.

In `packages/swift-sdk/Sources/SwiftDashSDK/FFI/PlatformQueryExtensions.swift`:
- [SUGGESTION] packages/swift-sdk/Sources/SwiftDashSDK/FFI/PlatformQueryExtensions.swift:1769-1781: Run the generic Swift contest lookups on the query queue
  The revised generic catalog can now send a complete poll key, but this `async` wrapper calls the synchronous network FFI inside an `@MainActor` extension. The UI stays blocked while DAPI responds or retries. The generic listing and voters wrappers do the same. Use `performBlockingQuery` to retain the SDK and copy and free the native response off the main actor, while preserving the existing empty-result behavior.
- [SUGGESTION] packages/swift-sdk/Sources/SwiftDashSDK/FFI/PlatformQueryExtensions.swift:1730-1734: Document when vote-state fields are absent
  The Swift docs group `winner_info` with the tallies, but an open poll can return contender counts without a winner. Lock and abstain tallies are omitted when not returned, and the native serializer now omits an unread contender `vote_count` instead of writing zero. Document those distinctions in Swift and in Kotlin's raw-JSON API so consumers decode missing values as optional rather than as zero.
- [SUGGESTION] packages/swift-sdk/Sources/SwiftDashSDK/FFI/PlatformQueryExtensions.swift:1686-1696: Include the stacked API changes in the migration notes
  The breaking-changes section covers the backslash rule, but the full diff also changes the native listing's `id` from base58 to an encoded index value and `index_values` from a string to a JSON array. Swift callers must replace `startAtValue:` with the index-value bounds and update the vote-state result names and return type from `[[String: Any]]` to `[String: Any]`. Summarize those changes here or link directly to the migration notes in #6033 so callers know which decoders and call sites to update.

In `packages/swift-sdk/SwiftExampleApp/SwiftExampleApp/Views/QueryDetailView.swift`:
- [BLOCKING] packages/swift-sdk/SwiftExampleApp/SwiftExampleApp/Views/QueryDetailView.swift:469-478: Keep DPNS contest addressing and name parsing in Rust
  (carried; thread: https://github.com/dashpay/platform/pull/6034#discussion_r4651948881)
```

<details>
<summary>Out-of-scope follow-up suggestions (1)</summary>

These are valid observations, but they are outside this PR's scope and should be handled in separate issues or author/maintainer-requested PRs rather than blocking this review.

- **Distinguish a page subtotal from the Kotlin poll total** — The Kotlin example already summed a single generic vote-state response and labeled it `Total Votes` on the base revision. An open poll with more contenders than the node returns in one page can therefore show a subtotal as the poll-wide total.
  - Follow-up: Use a complete, proof-verified Rust SDK read for the total, or label the displayed number as a subtotal when only one page was read.

</details>

**🔴 Blocking: Keep DPNS contest addressing and name parsing in Rust**

The revised DPNS catalog calls choose the DPNS contract, document type, index, and parent in Swift and pass them to the generic FFI. The new helper at lines 902–908 also implements case-insensitive `.dash` suffix recognition in the view because the label bridge only performs homograph conversion. The book’s “Where code goes” and “FFI and mobile SDKs hold no business logic” rules put these decisions in Rust. `rs-sdk/src/platform/dpns_usernames/contested_queries.rs` already owns the typed DPNS listing and vote-state addressing, and `normalize_dpns_label` already parses bare and full names. Use the existing DPNS listing export and thin bindings to Rust-owned poll construction and name normalization for the DPNS-specific operations. Keep the generic catalog entries generic.
